title: Which other country do you think lives almost entirely along one river?
desc: Egypt covers about 1 million km², but about 95% of its people live in a narrow strip along the Nile and its delta, which is only about 5% of the country's land. The Western Desert alone covers about two-thirds of Egypt. Watch the full story on YouTube: Map Behind History. #egypt #nile #history #geography #maps

title: Would you take the 35-minute ferry from Europe to Africa? Where would you go first?
desc: At its narrowest the Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe and Africa by about 14 km, and it is the gateway between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Around 6 million years ago the connection closed completely and salt deposits formed; about 5.33 million years ago it reopened and has stayed open since. title: Have you walked any part of Hadrian's Wall? Which stretch would you recommend?
desc: In AD 122 Emperor Hadrian ordered a wall across northern Britain: 73 miles (80 Roman miles) from Wallsend on the Tyne to Bowness-on-Solway, built by soldiers of three legions in about six years and up to about 15 feet tall. A gated milecastle stood roughly every Roman mile, with two turrets between each pair, plus larger forts. title: Would you sail to Point Nemo just to say you'd been to the loneliest spot on Earth?
desc: Point Nemo, the oceanic pole of inaccessibility in the South Pacific, is about 2,688 km from the nearest land: Ducie Island, Motu Nui near Easter Island, and Maher Island off Antarctica. Survey engineer Hrvoje Lukatela first calculated its position in 1992 and named it after Jules Verne's Captain Nemo (Latin for 'nobody'). title: Why Does Brazil Speak Portuguese? The 1494 Line
desc: On 7 June 1494, at Tordesillas in Spain, Castile and Portugal agreed a line from pole to pole, 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands: new lands to the west for Castile, to the east for Portugal. It moved the line set by Pope Alexander VI's 1493 bull, 100 leagues out. Later maps placed the line anywhere from about 42° to 50° W. Watch the full story on YouTube: Map Behind History. #treatyoftordesillas #1494 #history #geography #maps

title: Why Chile Is So Long and Thin
desc: Chile runs 4,270 km from north to south but is only 177 km wide on average. The two halves of that shape have two different explanations: the Andes made Chile thin, and nearly four centuries of conquest, war and treaties made it long. Watch the full story on YouTube: Map Behind History. #chile #whyischilesolong #history #geography #maps

title: How Istanbul Ended Up on Two Continents
desc: Istanbul spans Europe and Asia across the Bosphorus. Greek settlers from Megara first founded Chalcedon on the Asian shore; according to Strabo, an oracle later told the founders of Byzantium to build "opposite the blind", which they took to mean Chalcedon, and they settled the far better European site.
